PullRequest.Title: show slight color when side chat is not focused
PullRequest.Body: before vs. after cc @mrleemurray

Scenarios.Scenario: Hovering or keyboard-focusing an inactive session or split chat, then leaving it
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing hover/focus selectors and active-group class changes cause browser style resolution and paint. The request fill and border now join the existing 100 ms reveal animation; no asynchronous operation must finish before interaction can proceed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Browser style interpolation and painting of request background colors and zero-blur inset outlines
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two additional custom-property transition tracks per affected list for 100 ms; outline painting applies to matching rendered request bubbles and origin chips. Existing request background and response opacity interpolation already ran over the same subtree.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The list already animated opacity and an inherited bubble-background property for 100 ms. Request background colors already changed each animation frame; request outlines were absent.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Visual reveal occurs during browser rendering, without new script-driven geometry reads or changes to row dimensions.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Rendered descendant DOM in the affected chat lists, including request markdown and origin chips. ListView normally renders the viewport range rather than the entire history; a current text selection can extend that range.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Browser-managed transitions can run simultaneously on affected lists. No new task queue, request fan-out, or persistent animation loop; unchanged motion gating disables transitions under reduced motion.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No application cache is added or invalidated. Cold and warm interaction use the same selectors; existing render-row reuse is unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the added transition and paint operations from the CSS and endpoint/intermediate-state assertions. No evidence establishes a substantial new rendering bottleneck beyond the existing animated subtree work.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual rendering time depends on rendered subtree complexity and hardware; no runtime profiling was available.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable high-confidence regression. The change adds bounded visual work to an already animated path without new layout feedback, blurred effects, or lifetime growth.

Scenarios.Scenario: Displaying and scrolling unfocused chat transcripts, including partially visible sticky requests and request-origin chips
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing virtualized tree rendering inserts and removes rows while scrolling. The CSS adds a size-preserving outline to requests and origins, with three nonblurred inset strokes on a partially visible sticky request. Optional origin-quote loading remains asynchronous and off the transcript's initial display path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Paint request outlines in normal and sticky tree rows
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One outline per matching rendered bubble/origin, with three strokes on at most one sticky row per chat tree; not one operation per historical turn.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same virtualized rows and sticky request were already rendered with request backgrounds but without the new outline.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Adds paint, but not geometry changes that would independently trigger dynamic-height relayout.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing optional local source-session restoration reads a log file, with flat-file or previous-location fallback
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero reads for a supplied selection or loaded source model. Each eligible local cache-miss restoration reads the log or flat representation; fallback can add reads. The PR does not change the number of restorations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical optional restoration, file reads, fallback behavior, and source-quote rendering.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Quote resolution is started with void after rendering the origin title; it does not block scrolling or initial transcript display.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Decode and revive a restored source-session log or JSON history
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per successful local cache-miss restoration, scaling with source-session data size; unchanged by the new styling.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same full source-session decode occurred on the same cache-miss path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Part of optional asynchronous quote resolution, not added to hover or outline rendering.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing remote source-session provider resolution through canResolveChatSession and getOrCreateChatSession
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Loaded model hits avoid provider resolution. Concurrent remote misses join the in-flight load keyed by session resource; distinct source resources can load independently.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical remote model reuse, per-resource in-flight coalescing, and provider requests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Optional quote resolution remains off the initial transcript display path. Provider-specific downstream IPC/network implementation is unchanged and was not expanded into unrelated code.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Request bubbles and origin chips in the current render range; stickyScrollMaxItemCount is 1. Source loading is attempted only for origins lacking a supplied selection and an already loaded source model.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing scroll rendering stays on the UI thread. Local source reads are serialized by storeQueue; remote loads coalesce per key, not globally. All asynchronous source-loading scheduling is unchanged.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Viewport row reuse is unchanged. Origins use a supplied selection or existing model before loading. Remote loads coalesce by resource and settled entries are removed; local reads use the existing store queue. The diff changes no positive/negative cache behavior or retention.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from ListView render-range insertion/removal, sticky-row limits, and the traced origin-resolution path that the diff neither increases session-loading cardinality nor changes row geometry.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Paint magnitude depends on visible request complexity and selection-expanded render ranges. Provider-specific load duration is irrelevant to causality because loading is unchanged.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Bounded nonblurred outline painting does not establish scroll jank; existing filesystem, provider, and serialization work is not caused or amplified by this CSS-only production change.

Scenarios.Scenario: Using active chats, comparison-grid mode, high-contrast themes, or reduced motion
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Browser selector evaluation determines styling when mode, theme, or active-group state changes. Active chats, comparison grids, and high-contrast modes are excluded from the new outline rules; reduced motion excludes the transition rule.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Mounted session lists and their rendered descendants when application classes change; no new collection traversal in application code.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing synchronous class/style updates followed by browser rendering; no new asynchronous tasks or boundary calls.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No changed cache or model lifecycle. Theme colors still come from the existing in-memory theme lookup and CSS variables.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from explicit selector exclusions and tests asserting active/comparison/high-contrast absence of outlines, unchanged bubble dimensions, and zero reduced-motion animations.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No measured theme-switch or activation latency; no concrete added scaling mechanism was found for the excluded modes.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression established. Tests and fixture descriptions cover visual behavior, and the stylelint variable inventory is build-time metadata rather than added product-path work.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass over all four changed files and every diff page against base 733a99842b0e0e14c3593dfab31fff2035478ba0. Traced CSS animation/paint, virtualized scrolling and sticky rows, active-state callers, and unchanged optional source-session I/O/serialization. No high-confidence actionable performance regression or concrete regression fix found. Static read-only review; the supporting guide tool output was truncated, while the learned-mechanism document and supplied focus instructions were available.
